title: A Choir for the Ember Anew
premise: Astrid Eastwick, a runaway apprentice hiding his gift in the smuggler's roads of the Thornfell mountains, is captured by the crown's witch-hunters and offered a bargain: use his rare ember-sight to locate the last living members of an ancient covenant between the human realm and the fading fae Emberlands. As he gathers the scattered covenant-bearers, he discovers the hunt is a cover for a court faction that wants the covenant broken forever so the crown can drain the Emberlands' magic to survive a coming blight. Astrid must choose between exposing his own identity to save the fae or staying hidden while both realms starve; in the end he reforges the covenant at the cost of his own gift, becoming the bridge between realms rather than a wielder of power.
about_author: Wendell Nystrom is a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction, and his love of liminal places saturates every borderland he writes. He lives quietly at the edge of a forest that he insists, politely, is ordinary.

chapters.title: Salt on the Smuggler's Road
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. He guides contraband through the Thornfell passes using subtle hedge-magic, hiding his gift even from his crew. When a checkpoint nearly exposes him, he burns a memory-charm on a fellow smuggler to escape. Emotional beat: the loneliness of constant concealment, and the first hint that his lies are costing him pieces of himself.

chapters.title: The Proclamation at Millbrook Cross
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A royal crier announces the Gift-Hunt: all bearers of the old blood must register or be taken. Astrid watches a neighbor's daughter dragged away and does nothing. Emotional beat: shame crystallizing into resolve — he will run deeper into the mountains, but the seed of guilt is planted.

chapters.title: What the Apprentice Left Behind
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Astrid's POV: his years with the hedge-witch Maren, her warning that his ember-sight marks him as a covenant-keeper's heir, and the night he fled rather than accept a destiny he never chose. Emotional beat: understanding that his flight was fear dressed as freedom.

chapters.title: Hunted Through the White Pass
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Witch-hunters with sniffer-hounds corner him in a snowbound pass. He is saved by Sylwen, a fae exile disguised as a wandering tinker, who kills two hunters and vanishes. Emotional beat: terror giving way to wonder — proof the Emberlands still reach into the world.

chapters.title: The Bargain at Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, meeting Lord-Captain Drevane for the first time. Captured at last, Astrid is offered a deal instead of the pyre: serve as the hunt's tracker, or burn. Drevane is courteous, reasonable, and utterly ruthless. Emotional beat: the sick relief of survival purchased with complicity.

chapters.title: Ember-Sight
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Forced to use his gift for the crown, he sees the land's magic guttering like a dying fire — and realizes the blight threatening both realms is real. He also glimpses Sylwen watching from afar. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread as he understands the stakes are larger than his own neck.

chapters.title: The First Bearer
chapters.summary: Alternating Astrid/Sylwen POVs. Tracking a covenant-bearer, Astrid deliberately misleads the hunters and warns the target — old ferryman Corvin — instead. Sylwen reveals the covenant's history and asks his help reforging it. Emotional beat: the first open act of rebellion, thrilling and irreversible.

chapters.title: Drevane's Patience
chapters.summary: Drevane's POV. The captain suspects Astrid's treachery but lets the leash slack, believing the apprentice will lead him to every bearer at once. We see the court faction's true aim: harvest the Emberlands' magic. Emotional beat: cold dread — the reader now knows the trap's shape before Astrid does.

chapters.title: Road of Ashes
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A burned village where a bearer was taken alive shows what failure costs. Astrid finds a child survivor and smuggles her along the old roads, his smuggling skills finally turned to sanctuary rather than profit. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Choir Gathers
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. At a hidden waystation, three bearers assemble: Corvin, blind seer Ivetta, and disgraced court mage Tam. Their voices literally harmonize, stirring dormant ember-light. Emotional beat: cautious hope — a fragile found-family forming around a shared song.

chapters.title: Sylwen's Exile
chapters.summary: Sylwen's POV. Her backstory: she broke Emberlands law by loving a human, and her exile left the covenant unguarded when it shattered. She confesses this to Astrid by firelight. Emotional beat: intimacy built on mutual guilt; loyalty deepening into something neither names.

chapters.title: The Trap at Greywater Ford
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Drevane springs his trap; Ivetta is captured and the child hostage threatened. Astrid bargains himself back into custody to spare them, concealing the others' location at terrible personal risk. Emotional beat: the price of survival made flesh — he buys their safety with his own chains.

chapters.title: Chains and Cages
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV in the capital's witch-cells. He endures interrogation by Inquisitor Hale, who probes not for locations but for the nature of his gift. A sympathetic jailer smuggles out a message via ember-light. Emotional beat: endurance, and the discovery that even caged, he is not powerless.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Dragged before the Regent, he witnesses the harvesting engine being built from stolen covenant-stones. He learns the blight is partly manufactured to justify the hunt. Emotional beat: righteous fury replacing fear — the enemy is not fate but ambition.

chapters.title: Tam's Betrayal
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Pressured by threats to his family, the disgraced mage sells the choir's location to Drevane — then drowns in regret. Emotional beat: tragedy of loyalty vs. truth; betrayal born of love, not malice.

chapters.title: Ride of the Tinker
chapters.summary: Sylwen's POV. She breaks Astrid from the cells with help from the jailer and Corvin's river-craft, revealing her full fae form at last. They flee the burning capital as alarms rise. Emotional beat: exhilaration and tenderness — rescue as declaration.

chapters.title: The Broken Covenant-Stone
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. At the ruined covenant-site, the survivors find the great stone sundered; reforging it demands a bearer surrender their gift entirely. Each member offers; each is refused by the stone. Emotional beat: despair — sacrifice alone is not enough.

chapters.title: What Astrid Is
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Ivetta's final vision reveals the truth: Astrid is not merely a bearer but the covenant's intended keystone, born of both lineages — Maren's secret he fled. Emotional beat: the identity theme cresting; the thing he ran from is the thing he is.

chapters.title: The Harvesting Rises
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Drevane activates the engine; the Emberlands begin to die visibly — rivers silvering, fae lights failing. Sylwen starts to fade. The army marches on the covenant-site. Emotional beat: ticking-clock desperation; time has run out.

chapters.title: Battle of the Sundered Stone
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The choir fights holding actions while Astrid reaches the stone; Corvin falls buying him seconds, and Tam redeems himself by shattering the engine at cost of his life. Emotional beat: costly heroism — every victory paid for in blood.

chapters.title: A Choir for the Ember Anew
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. At the stone, Astrid surrenders his gift willingly — not as loss but as offering — and the covenant reforges with his ember-sight woven into the land itself, ending the blight and halting the harvest. Drevane, seeing the realms renewed, stands down rather than slay the source of the crown's salvation. Emotional beat: transcendence through surrender.

chapters.title: The Bridge Between
chapters.summary: Epilogue, shifting POVs. Months later: the borders open, Sylwen no longer exiled, the rescued child apprenticed to rebuilt hedge-craft. Astrid, giftless but sighted in new ways, walks the old smuggler's roads as an envoy between realms. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — he lost his magic and found his place.
